title: Eosin Methylene Blue Agar

references.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

purpose: Selects for Gram-negative enteric bacteria while inhibiting most Gram-positive organisms, and differentiates strong lactose fermenters (which can show a characteristic metallic green sheen) from weak or non-fermenters.

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

preparationSummary: Suspend the dehydrated powder per the manufacturer's stated concentration, heat with agitation to boiling to fully dissolve, then sterilize and pour while still liquid, mixing gently before pouring since the dyes can settle.
storage: Refrigerate prepared plates in sealed bags, protected from light.
expectedAppearance: Dark purple to nearly black opaque agar due to the eosin and methylene blue dyes.
qualityControl: Verify selectivity (a Gram-positive control should be inhibited) and differentiation (a strong lactose fermenter should show dark colonies with a green metallic sheen; a non-fermenter should appear colorless to amber) against reference organisms.

reactions.organismOrGroup: Strong lactose fermenters producing large amounts of acid (e.g. many E. coli strains)
reactions.reaction: Dark blue-black colonies, often with a distinctive green metallic sheen
Pink to mucoid colonies without the metallic sheen

reactions.organismOrGroup: Non-lactose fermenters (e.g. many Salmonella, Shigella strains)

manufacturerNotes: The green metallic sheen is a classic presumptive indicator associated with E. coli but is not itself confirmatory identification; formulation details (e.g. exact lactose/sucrose content) vary between manufacturers and affect how pronounced the sheen appears.
